note: Who a reveal is for (AUD-2, ED-10, owner decision O-3): the whole table, or ONE OR MORE participants by id. A reveal to one player is a list of one; there is no separate singular shape, because a group display is per-recipient copies of one disclosure. A named group is expanded by the client into its member ids at the moment the GM confirms, exactly as `all` is expanded into field keys (ED-8), so no group id and no wildcard ever travels or is stored and a group whose membership changes later cannot silently widen a live reveal. An audience is an identity, never a credential and never an alias (AUD-11). Nothing here ties an audience to a document type: owner decision O-2 makes a participant audience legal for ANY type, and the registry's `audience` flag now says only whose default reveal a type seeds. A SLOT names one participant, not a list (RevealSlotRef); a table client is never told either (SEC-15). Since a slot got its own shape, an audience travels in one place only — `RevealRequest.audience` — so this file is tagged `request`: an undeclared key, `__proto__` included, is a finding on both sides rather than the recorded response asymmetry.

valid.name: three participants, one disclosure in three copies

invalid.name: an empty recipient list
invalid.why: O-3: a disclosure has at least one copy; an empty list is a Stop wearing a Confirm's shape

invalid.name: the same participant twice
invalid.why: a recipient list is a set: a repeat would mean two copies of one disclosure for one participant, and a slot is listed once

invalid.name: an alias beside the recipient list
invalid.why: AUD-11: an alias is a display name and never leaves the GM's channel, so it is refused even where the ids beside it are correct — there is no member it could ride in

invalid.name: a display name where an id belongs
invalid.why: ED-10: an audience is an identity, and a display name with a space is not an opaque id. An alias that happens to match the id alphabet cannot be told from an id by shape — that is inherent in opaque ids, and is why the server resolves every id against the session's own participants (SEC-3)

invalid.name: a recipient list beside the table audience
invalid.why: the table is not a list of participants; one shape per audience, and no half-named disclosure

invalid.name: the singular participant shape
invalid.why: owner decision O-3 replaced it: a reveal to one player is a list of one, so there is exactly one shape for every private disclosure and `stop all copies` never has a special case

invalid.name: a recipient list with no ids field
invalid.why: ED-10: a participant audience is an identity; there is nothing to evaluate without one

invalid.name: a bare string
invalid.why: an audience is a discriminated object, so a second kind cannot be added by string

invalid.name: an audience kind this contract does not define
invalid.why: closed vocabulary: a group is expanded into participant ids by the client (ED-8), so a group audience is not a value this wire ever carries

invalid.name: a participant id outside the id alphabet
